The implementation is in [output_model_new.py](/root/lumen-clean/lumen-sosp26-ae-origin/runs/kernelbench_generation_level1_moonbridge_no_examples/p98/round0/output_model_new.py). Two kernels handle the KL divergence:

1. **`kl_div_row_kernel`** — 16,384 blocks, one per row. Each block's 256 threads stripe across the 16,384 columns, loading BF16 values and accumulating `target * (log(target) - log(prediction))` in FP32. A shared-memory tree reduction (grouped by wavefront-64 on AMD) collapses each row to a single FP32 partial sum.

2. **`final_reduce_kernel`** — single block sums the 16,384 per-row partials and divides by batch size, matching the `batchmean` reduction.

The one gotcha was output dtype: when the harness feeds BF16 inputs, PyTorch's eager `kl_div` returns BF16, so the wrapper converts the FP32 accumulation result back to the input dtype with `.to(predictions.dtype)`.
